queue_objective.derivation_point: 1.0x per-delay reference capacity, query arm, open loop
queue_objective.model_guidance: M/M/1/K with K waiting slots (system capacity K+1) at rho=1 blocks 1/(K+2): K=0 -> 1/2, K=1 -> 1/3, K=2 -> 1/4; admitted wait bounded by K x mean S, far below the 100 ms budget for every level
queue_objective.zero_delay_1x: All arms zero terminal rejection, sub-0.11 ms p95; the objective does not distinguish K.
queue_objective.five_ms_1x_198_per_s: Now executable. hygiene-only terminal blocking 0.187, p95 585.2 ms. A K=1: blocking 0, A 1.01, p95 10.0 ms, permit-wait p95 4.94 ms. K=2: blocking 0, p95 11.1 ms, permit-wait p95 6.12 ms.
queue_objective.twenty_five_ms_1x_40_per_s: hygiene-only terminal blocking 0.163, p95 541.4 ms. A K=1: blocking 0, A 1.0, p95 28.5 ms, permit-wait p95 3.51 ms. K=2: blocking 0, p95 28.7 ms, permit-wait p95 3.70 ms.
queue_objective.baseline_strict_note: Pre-change baseline has zero terminal blocking at 1.0x because it retries without an attempt budget (amplification 3.11-4.21, p95 0.58-1.07 s). Against the hygiene-only reference arm, K=1 removes terminal blocking entirely. K=1 is the smallest K whose model-guided blocking (1/3) improves on the measured baseline attempt-level rejection and whose model-guided p95 wait is below 100 ms.

tradeoffs_recorded: C imposes its ~2 ms fast-first delay on already-ready batch paths: zero-delay closed-1 p95 rises 0.18->2.29 ms (1x16) and 0.35->2.44 ms (1x64)
C raises voluntary context switches (~2x at 25 ms S, ~3.7x at 5 ms S on closed-1 batch cells) and adds up to 3 polls at the overload tail
at 2x query overload a+c terminally rejects slightly more than A alone (29-30 vs 20-23 of 80) while cutting p95 from ~620 ms to ~330 ms; both are explicit bounded queue_full behavior
